componentPlan.focusQuote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Introduces free fall as motion under weight alone with constant acceleration before checking facts

componentPlan.focusQuote: The remarkable observation that all free falling objects fall at the same rate was first proposed by Galileo, nearly 400 years ago.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks memorable facts about same rate fall and Galileo observation after modeling motion

overview.headline: Free fall in a vacuum accelerates constantly due to gravity

keyPoints.point: Free falling means moving only because of gravity with weight as the only external force in a vacuum
keyPoints.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.

keyPoints.point: Free fall acceleration stays constant at gravitational acceleration at sea level on Earth
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyPoints.point: Acceleration remains constant while velocity grows linearly and location grows quadratically over time
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.

keyPoints.point: Galileo proposed that all free falling objects fall at the same rate regardless of mass
keyPoints.quote: The remarkable observation that all free falling objects fall at the same rate was first proposed by Galileo, nearly 400 years ago.

keyTerms.gloss: moving only because of gravity action
keyTerms.quote: An object that is moving only because of the action of gravity is said to be free falling

keyTerms.gloss: constant acceleration due to gravity at sea level
keyTerms.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: gravitational force expressed as weight of object
keyTerms.quote: The weight, size, and shape of the object are not a factor in describing a free fall.

keyTerms.gloss: additional force acting on object in atmosphere
keyTerms.quote: there is an additional drag force acting on the object

keyTerms.gloss: different fall speeds when air resistance balances motion
keyTerms.quote: they are subject to air resistance and would fall at different terminal velocities

analysis.pageCoverage: Covers free fall in a vacuum under weight alone, constant gravitational acceleration with velocity and displacement relations, a table of values over time, and Galileo finding on same rate fall
